howDoI.q: How do I let my hero throw something?
How do I make a thrown star pop a monster?
How do I make a thrown star fly only so far?
How do I choose which way a thrown star flies?
How do I make a monster that blocks the way until it is popped?

pages.head: Welcome
pages.html:
Welcome

Throw It is a Starter: a small game that shows a few Game-Maker ideas, with signs in the levels that say what you are looking at. It has two short levels and takes a couple of minutes to finish.

Play it first. Then open it in Game-Maker (Edit a copy on the home page keeps the original safe) and read the pages below, which say where each thing in the levels is made.

The keys

Left and Right walk. Space jumps. Enter throws a star. F2 shows your lives, hit points and score. Walk into the door at the end of a level to go on.

A star flies the way you last walked, so walk toward what you want to pop, then throw. Nothing in this game hurts you.

pages.head: Level 1: Throw a Star
pages.html:
Level 1: Throw a Star

The PRESS ENTER TO THROW A STAR sign stands before a mint green gumdrop that sits still. Walk up to it and press Enter: Kit swings his arm, a gold star spins away from his hand, and when it touches the gumdrop the gumdrop pops into a little sparkle for 50 points. Touching the gumdrop yourself does nothing, so it is the star that pops it.

The A STAR FLIES ONLY SO FAR sign stands before a second gumdrop that is a long way off. A star thrown from here runs out of time and twinkles away before it gets there. Walk closer, about five blocks away, and throw again.

There are six coins on the way, worth ten points each.

pages.head: How this level is made
pages.html:
How level 1 is made

  • The key. Open hero.chr in the character editor and pick the Throw sequence. Its key is Enter. Once per key press is on, so holding the key throws one star, not a stream. Always finish the sequence is on, so the arm always swings through.
  • The throw. The sequence has four frames. The first two show Kit winding up and letting go. The third is not a picture: its Frame action is Give birth to monster, and the monster is number 3, the star. The fourth shows him following through. The birth comes with no pause, so the star appears just as the hand opens.
  • Which way it flies. A monster born this way flies the way the hero last moved. Kit starts a level facing right. After you walk left it flies left. After a jump it flies up, until you take a step. The star cannot hurt Kit.
  • The star. Open throw.mon in the monsters editor and pick the star. Its Movement is chases the character at speed 4, which for a born monster means flying away at 4 pixels a tick. It is Stopped by solid blocks, so a wall ends it. Its Power is 200, higher than a gumdrop's 150. Its life is 30 ticks, so it flies about six blocks and then becomes a sparkle: the For a set time setting is what makes a star fall short.
  • The pop. When two monsters touch, the weaker one is destroyed. The star is the stronger one, and because the character threw it, it is used up as well. The destroyed gumdrop gives the hero its Score when destroyed by a weapon, 50, and plays Game-Maker's kill sound. Both turn into the sparkle named in When destroyed it becomes.
  • Why touching does nothing. A monster below Power 100 is destroyed when the hero touches it. The gumdrop's Power is 150, so the hero walks through it harmlessly and only a star pops it.
  • The signs. Each sign is a few ordinary blocks side by side, with the words drawn in their pictures. Change the words in the blocks editor and play again.
  • The walls. The room is closed in by brick walls at both ends, and the exit door links to the next level in throw.gam.

pages.head: Level 2: The Narrow Way
pages.html:
Level 2: The Narrow Way

The A GRUMP BLOCKS THE NARROW WAY sign stands before a brick wall with a low tunnel through it, and a purple grump sitting in the tunnel with no room to go around. Walk into it and Kit stops: the grump is solid. It does not hurt, it just does not move.

The A STAR FLIES THE WAY YOU LAST WALKED sign says what to do. Step back to the left and throw, and the star flies left, away from the grump, and twinkles out. Walk toward the tunnel and throw again, and the grump pops for 50 points and the way is open.

There are six coins, two before the tunnel and four after.

pages.head: How this level is made
pages.html:
How level 2 is made

  • The narrow way. Open two.map in the map editor. The tunnel is two blocks high, the hero's own height, cut through a wall of brick that goes up to the top of the room. There is no room to jump over the grump and no way around it.
  • A monster that blocks. Monsters are not solid unless their picture is. Open throw.mbl in the blocks editor and look at guard0 and guard1: their Solid boxes are checked on every side, which holds the hero back from walking through. The kit's gumdrops and the mint ones from level 1 are not solid, so he walks through those.
  • Harmless to touch. The grump's pictures take no hit points. Its Power is 150, so touching it does not destroy it either. Only a star can clear it.
  • Which way it flies. The same Throw sequence as level 1. The star goes the way Kit last walked, so a step to the left before throwing sends it left. Walk toward the grump first. This is also why the sign says it.
  • Where the star starts. The birth frame sits in the hero's own row, so a star flies straight along the ground. It cannot be aimed higher or lower in this game.
  • Clearing the way. When the star and the grump touch, both are destroyed and become sparkles that last half a second. The grump's Score when destroyed by a weapon is 50.
  • The exit. The last door links to the The End scene in throw.gam, which plays the ending.

pages.head: Make it yours
pages.html:
Make it yours

Try one change at a time, and play after each:

  • Change the star's Speed, or its Lifetime, to make it fly faster or farther.
  • Redraw the star: its pictures are star0 and star1 in throw.mbl.
  • Change the Power of the grump to 250. Now the star cannot pop it, and the way is shut.
  • Move the throw to another key in the Throw sequence's Key setting.
  • Put a second grump in the tunnel and see how many stars it takes.

The home page's Starters tab has more small games like this one.
